name: Kim Min-jun
action: Min-jun confirms the coding test dates by replying to the recruiter's email, then calls his mother-in-law and asks her to cover Seo-yeon's vaccination on the second day, providing the appointment time and details so the handoff is clear.
reason: Min-jun's initial impulse was to accept the test dates and call his mother-in-law for backup care, despite his reluctance to burden her again. Reflective reappraisal strengthened this tendency: he weighed asking the recruiter to shift the test, but his memory of past offers withdrawn after he raised scheduling constraints made that seem too risky. He framed the conflict as a scheduling collision with asymmetric risks—keeping the test dates protects a job that could provide extended parental leave, while the vaccination will still occur either way. He accepted the lower-risk path despite the lingering guilt about leaving his daughter's care to his mother-in-law and the echo of his own father's absence. The final action—confirming the dates and arranging coverage—directly follows his revised tendency, prioritizing candidacy security over visible hands-on caregiving.
